trap.title: Cemetery, house, or county?
trap.body: Several answers share the name Arlington. Arlington House is the Lee family’s mansion on the cemetery grounds, Arlington County is the Virginia county around it (home of the Pentagon), and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is one memorial inside the cemetery. On this answer line, plain “Arlington” or “Arlington County” earns only a prompt, and “Arlington House” or the Tomb alone is wrong.
trap.fix: When a tossup says “this cemetery,” answer “Arlington National Cemetery.” If it asks for “this mansion” (Custis, Lee, Greek Revival columns), say Arlington House; if it asks for “this memorial” guarded by the Old Guard, say the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
trap.line: Real answer line: Arlington National Cemetery (accept Arlington Cemetery; prompt on Arlington or Arlington County; do not accept “Arlington House”)

topics.name: Bacon’s Rebellion
topics.kicker: 1676 revolt against Virginia’s governor · Rebels burned Jamestown
topics.briefing: In 1676, a 29-year-old planter named Nathaniel Bacon led angry frontier settlers, servants, and some enslaved Africans in a revolt against Virginia’s governor, William Berkeley. The rebels attacked Native peoples, including some who had been at peace with the colony, and burned the capital, Jamestown, to the ground. The revolt fell apart after Bacon died of disease, and many historians think it pushed Virginia’s planters to rely more on enslaved labor.

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: In 1675, a quarrel over trade goods between a planter in northern Virginia and the Doeg people led to killings on the frontier. Soon afterward, Virginia and Maryland militias killed five Susquehannock [“suss-kwuh-HAN-uk”] leaders who had come out to negotiate, and raids and counterattacks spread along the frontier.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1676 revolt in which Nathaniel Bacon led frontier settlers against Governor William Berkeley.

tossups.p: In May 1676, a planter led volunteers to an island in the Roanoke River, where they persuaded the Occaneechi [“oh-kuh-NEE-chee”] people to attack the Susquehannock and then turned on the Occaneechi themselves. Virginia’s governor declared that planter a rebel for marching without permission.
tossups.r: That planter was Nathaniel Bacon. For 10 points, name this 1676 uprising in colonial Virginia.

tossups.p: In June 1676, after the armed followers of this uprising’s leader surrounded the statehouse, a governor reportedly bared his chest and dared the leader to shoot him. The governor then gave the leader a commission to fight Native Americans.
tossups.r: That governor was William Berkeley. For 10 points, name this rebellion in Virginia, led by Nathaniel Bacon.

tossups.p: On July 30, 1676, the leader of this event issued a “Declaration in the Name of the People” that accused Virginia’s governor of unjust taxes, rewarding his favorites, and failing to defend settlers on the frontier.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1676 rebellion in which Nathaniel Bacon’s followers burned Jamestown.

tossups.p: A House of Burgesses that met in June 1676 passed reforms named for the leader of this uprising, including a law that again allowed free men who owned no land to vote. The king’s government later canceled those reforms.
tossups.r: That leader was Nathaniel Bacon. For 10 points, name this 1676 rebellion against Virginia governor William Berkeley.

tossups.p: During this event, a governor fled across the Chesapeake Bay to Accomack County on Virginia’s Eastern Shore, where he gathered loyal men and ships before returning to fight. His plantation, Green Spring, stood just a few miles from the capital.
tossups.r: That governor was William Berkeley. For 10 points, name this 1676 revolt led by Nathaniel Bacon.

tossups.p: Rebels held a brick house in Surry County for several months during this event, and the house is still named for their leader, even though he never went there. Built in 1665, it is one of the oldest brick houses in the United States.
tossups.r: That leader was Nathaniel Bacon. For 10 points, name this 1676 rebellion in colonial Virginia.

tossups.p: After this event, King Charles II reportedly complained that his governor had hanged more men in Virginia than the king had executed for the killing of his own father. That governor had 23 rebels hanged before he was called back to England.
tossups.r: That governor was William Berkeley. For 10 points, name this 1676 revolt led by Nathaniel Bacon.

tossups.p: In his book _American Slavery, American Freedom_, historian Edmund Morgan argued that after this event, Virginia’s wealthy planters came to rely more on enslaved Africans and less on poor white servants, many of whom had joined it.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1676 rebellion against Governor William Berkeley, led by Nathaniel Bacon.

tossups.p: The Treaty of Middle Plantation, signed in 1677 after this event, made peace between Virginia and several Native nations, including the Pamunkey, whose leader was a woman the English called the Queen of Pamunkey. Her people had been attacked during this event.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this rebellion of 1676, led by Nathaniel Bacon against Virginia’s governor.

tossups.p: The leader of this event died of disease in October 1676 at age 29, and his body was never found; his followers may have buried it in secret. Joseph Ingram took over, but the revolt soon fell apart.
tossups.r: That leader was Nathaniel Bacon. For 10 points, name this rebellion in which Jamestown was burned.

tossups.p: King Charles II sent about 1,000 soldiers and three commissioners, including Herbert Jeffreys, to Virginia in response to this event. The colony’s longtime governor was ordered back to England, where he died in 1677, and Jeffreys took over the government.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this rebellion in which Nathaniel Bacon’s followers burned Jamestown, Virginia’s capital.

tossups.p: Near the end of this event, some of the last rebels holding out were enslaved Africans and English indentured servants who had joined it hoping to win their freedom. A ship captain named Thomas Grantham talked them into giving up.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1676 Virginia uprising led by Nathaniel Bacon against Governor William Berkeley.

tossups.p: The leader of this event had arrived in Virginia only in 1674, bought land along the James River, and was quickly given a seat on the governor’s council. In 1676, his overseer was killed in a raid on his frontier plantation.
tossups.r: That leader, Nathaniel Bacon, then led settlers against Governor William Berkeley. For 10 points, name this 1676 revolt.

tossups.p: A 1676 law backed by a colonial governor called for a line of expensive forts along the frontier, which many settlers saw as costly and useless. Some settlers also believed the governor wanted to protect his friends’ profitable fur trade with Native peoples.
tossups.r: Those settlers wanted war instead, and Nathaniel Bacon led them against Governor William Berkeley. For 10 points, name this 1676 rebellion.

trap.title: Rebel or rebellion?
trap.body: Nathaniel Bacon is the man and Bacon’s Rebellion is the event, so saying just his name earns only a prompt. Players also mix up colonial uprisings: Bacon’s Rebellion (1676, Virginia) is different from Leisler’s Rebellion (1689–1691, New York), the Stono Rebellion (1739, South Carolina), Shays’ Rebellion (1786–1787, Massachusetts), and the Whiskey Rebellion (1791–1794, Pennsylvania). King Philip’s War was raging in New England at the same time, but it was a separate conflict.
trap.fix: Virginia, 1676, Governor William Berkeley, frontier attacks on Native peoples, and the burning of Jamestown mean Bacon’s Rebellion. If you are prompted after saying “Bacon,” add “Rebellion.”
